Note. N = 1,243. WLSMV estimation. The three-factor CFA is nested within the ESEM's implied covariance class as the case with zero cross-loadings, so the ESEM row reports a scaled difference test against it. The ESEM degrees of freedom reflect its rotation constraints. Latent factor correlations in the three-factor CFA are 0.76 (arts and leisure), 0.68 (arts and residual), and 0.59 (leisure and residual). RMSEA 90\% confidence intervals are [{..095, ..102}] (one-factor), [{..095, ..102}] (residual into arts), [{..093, ..100}] (residual into leisure), [{..092, ..099}] (three-factor), and [{..070, ..079}] (ESEM). Scaled difference tests use the Satorra-Bentler scaled statistic with per-model scaling factors.

Note. Oblimin-rotated pattern loadings, the regression weight of each item on each factor adjusting for the correlations among the factors, from an exploratory factor analysis (WLS estimation, distinct from the WLSMV estimator used elsewhere; N = 1,243). Bold entries mark each item's assigned factor. The EFA fits the 20 items adequately ($\chi^2(133) = 290.8, $p < .001$, $\text{TLI} = .911, $\text{RMSEA} = .080$ [{..076, ..084}]). The assigned target column reports the varimax assignment used as the ESEM targets. Factor correlations from the oblique solution are 0.19 (arts and leisure), -0.15 (arts and residual), and -0.01 (leisure and residual). The sign of the arts--residual correlation differs from the positive value in Table~\ref{tab:activities-esem} because oblimin assigns gardening and home repair to the arts factor, leaving a residual factor close to fast food alone, so that in this solution frequent arts attendance comes with slightly more frequent fast dining.
